title: MC Hammer had 200 people on payroll. Then the hits stopped.
description:
A mansion with gold gates, a staff of two hundred, and a payroll that did not care how the next record sold.

New video every day.

scenes.say: MC Hammer built a mansion with gold plated gates. Twelve million to buy it, thirty million more to rebuild it.
And he hired everyone. Dancers, singers, security, friends. At its peak the payroll ran to about two hundred people.
By his own account, a million dollars a month went out in wages.
Here is the trap. Income from records moves up and down. A payroll does not. It arrives on the same day whether the album sold or not.
When the hits slowed, the wages kept coming. In nineteen ninety six he filed for bankruptcy. Nine point six million in assets, thirteen point seven million in debts.
The mansion went. The staff went. What broke him was not the spending. It was the part of the spending that repeated.
A thing you buy once costs you once. A thing you commit to costs you every month, forever, whatever happens to your income.
